# Synthetic analytical paragraphs (V040-14)

Audience: defense counsel. Document type: attorney note. Status: draft for Defense Writing Studio. These paragraphs are not a filed paper, and they cite no verified case. The facts are fictional Example County demonstration text. Proposition and evidence identifiers point into `v04014_argument_packet.json`.

## Element

The charge sheet alleges that Riley Quinn took store property from Example Market with intent to deprive the owner of it (P-SYN-CHARGE, E-SYN-CHARGE). That sentence is an allegation. It is not an established record fact, and the sheet says so. The legal hinge is the taking, including the required intent. The only rule statement in this packet, P-SYN-RULE-UNVERIFIED, is a working description with status research_pending. It is not a citation, and it is not available as reliance_approved authority. Until that research is done, the note can frame the proof gap. It cannot brief the element as settled law.

## Exit accounts

Jordan Hale's interview says the person Hale knows as Riley Quinn walked out the front door with a closed paper bag, and Hale did not see what was inside (P-SYN-FRONT, E-SYN-INTERVIEW-A, page 2, line 5, with the bag sentences on lines 6 and 7). The transcript says Hale saw Quinn go out the side door, that the bag was open, and that the bag looked empty (P-SYN-SIDE, P-SYN-EMPTY, E-SYN-TRANSCRIPT-SIDE at page 14, line 6, and E-SYN-TRANSCRIPT-EMPTY at page 14, line 9). Transcript page 14, line 10 calls the other account an earlier interview. That label orders the two documents. It does not time the two departures. P-SYN-ONE-EXIT is the inference that the packet does not establish whether those accounts describe the same departure or different moments. Neither source says Hale described only one exit. One fair alternative is that Hale described two parts of one departure. Another is that the questions asked about different moments. Neither alternative is a finding. The State's best account treats the front-door statement and the video log as the departure, and treats the side-door lines as a detail or an impression. That account is preserved here because the defense theory is weaker if it hides the front-door statement. The side-door statement is likewise kept. The State's account does not establish occurrence order.

## Contents

The video log states that a person was at the front door at store-clock 14:02:00 and that the image does not show the contents of any bag (P-SYN-VIDEO, E-SYN-VIDEO). The clock offset was not checked, and the log does not name the person. The officer note states that the bag was not inventoried. It does not state a policy that required an inventory, and it does not state that the bag was lost, destroyed, or withheld (P-SYN-NO-INVENTORY, E-SYN-OFFICER). From those three sources the permissible inference is P-SYN-CONTENTS-UNKNOWN: this packet does not establish what the bag held. Hale's "looked empty" sentence qualifies that inference and stays in the account. It is an appearance, not an inventory, and it does not prove the bag was empty at the front door. The missing inventory also does not prove that anyone hid, lost, or withheld the bag. The untested proposition is the contents. The limitation is that a taking cannot be argued as proved from the charge sheet plus a closed bag.

## Intent

The difference between the front-door account and the side-door account is a reason to compare recordings and to prepare impeachment, once it is known whether they describe the same departure (P-SYN-ONE-EXIT). It is not proof that Hale intended to deceive (P-SYN-NO-DECEPTION-FINDING). Hale said Hale does not know why the two answers differ. That sentence does not describe a plan, a bias, or a motive, and this note does not supply one. The intent grade on this packet is an unresolved alternative. It is not negligence, error, confirmation bias, recklessness, or deliberate misconduct, because the record does not contain evidence proportionate to any of those labels. A later recording could support a narrower grade. Until it does, the honest recommendation is to investigate: obtain the interview recording, the pages around transcript page 14, the video file with a checked clock, and any inventory policy that actually exists (A-SYN-EXIT-ROUTE). What would force a narrower theory is a timed sequence showing one continuous exit, or an inventory or frame that shows the contents. What would force rejection of a deception theory is the same record that exists now, unless new evidence speaks to Hale's purpose. No psychological story is stated as fact.
